decisions.reason: As an adjacent sports-flooring system in the firm’s core domain, it is relatively cheap to keep available while post-launch demand remains only partly revealed.
A mobile arena floor is a strategic but project-based offering, so despite higher support costs the uncertainty after a disrupted 2020-2021 market still favors keeping the option open.
This second mobile arena floor looks somewhat redundant with other options, but because it serves the same core customer base management would likely wait longer before abandoning it.
A chevron parquet pattern is a low-cost line extension of existing wood-floor capabilities, so there is little reason to withdraw it quickly.

The squash court finish appears to be a narrower niche than the firm’s broader flooring lines, so with several other sports-floor options available management would be more likely to reallocate resources away from it.
Oak skirting is a simple complement to sports floors that can be kept in the portfolio at low cost and bundled with established products.
